_about: Nitrogen (1) + methanol (2): mole fraction solubility of nitrogen at 298.15 K and 101.325 kPa, from Boyer and Bircher (1960), as compiled in IUPAC SDS Vol. 10.

source.citation: F. L. Boyer, L. J. Bircher, The solubility of nitrogen, argon, methane, ethylene and ethane in normal primary alcohols, J. Phys. Chem. 64 (1960) 1330-1331
source.access: The original article is not open; its values are compiled in IUPAC Solubility Data Series Vol. 10, Nitrogen and Air (R. Battino, ed., Pergamon, 1982; copyright IUPAC), which IUPAC publishes as open access at iupac.github.io
source.tables: IUPAC Solubility Data Series Vol. 10 (1982) p 181 (PDF p 226), prepared by M. E. Derrick; x_1 x 10^3 = 0.279 at 298.15 K, P/kPa = 101.325 as the sheet's variable, the observed value from Boyer's dissertation (1959). The sheet says the total pressure of gas and solvent vapour was kept at one atm during the measurement and does not say whether the compiled x is at a nitrogen partial pressure of 1 atm; it is taken so, as the volume's other sheets and its evaluation state their values (the evaluator smoothed it with them, p 174), and it agrees with them (0.2739 and 0.273 x 10^-3 at 298.15 K). Estimated error: T 0.01 K, Ostwald coefficient 0.167 +- 0.003.
source.transcription: Read from the scanned page image (rendered at 110 dpi) and the PDF's text layer, which agree value by value. The person checking should compare each row with the page.

notes: x_1 is the mole fraction of nitrogen in the liquid at a partial pressure of nitrogen of 101.325 kPa (1 atm), as the compiler gives it; it is stored as p_1_kPa = 101.325 (the fit compares it with y_1 P of the bubble point at x_1). To be checked by a person against the page (AGENTS.md rule 4).
